parts.article:
A Brief History of Humans and Food
 
(A) During the journey from our hunter-gatherer ancestors to the present day, there have been three seismic changes that have impacted the food we eat: the discovery of cooking, the emergence of agriculture, and the invention of methods of preserving food. The 19th-century scientist Charles Darwin thought that cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man. All of us eat some raw food, such as fruit and vegetables, but the great majority of food we consume is cooked. Cooking can turn plants that are inedible into edible food by destroying toxic chemicals that plants often manufacture to protect themselves against attack by insects or other herbivorous animals. These toxic chemicals are referred to as “plant secondary compounds” because they are not directly involved in the plant's normal growth, development, and reproduction, and are produced purely as chemical defenses. They give many of the plants we consume, such as coffee or Brussels sprouts, their bitter taste.
 
(B) Cooked food is often more digestible because heat breaks down tough cellulose cell walls in plants or tough connective tissue in animals. Chewing raw turnip, a plate of uncooked rice, or a raw leg of lamb is much harder work than eating the cooked equivalent. The energy expended in chewing to break down the tough material is replaced by energy from the fuel used in cooking the food, so the ratio of energy gained to energy expended by the body is greater when food is cooked.
 
(C) Until the development of agriculture, hunter-gatherers spent up to seven hours a day gathering food. This all began to change around 10,500 years ago with the advent of farming, which led to dramatic changes in human societies. People began to create a variety of new tools to aid survival, and in turn, populations increased in size. These changes led to the possibility of specialization of different tasks within society. Around this time, writing became more sophisticated and allowed people to maintain records of the harvest and taxes. Eventually, formalized structures of government were established as people settled in one area.
 
(D) The arrival of agriculture meant that, for the first time, our ancestors had more food than they could eat immediately. This, combined with the seasonality of production, led them to discover methods of preserving food: smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt. These four methods all share one feature in common—they make the food a more hostile environment for bacteria that can cause it to spoil. They also tend to slow down natural chemical reactions in the food that would cause decay.
 
(E) Although foods today are still preserved in these ancient ways, two more recent methods of preserving food have become more common: canning and freezing. Canning was invented by a Frenchman, Nicolas Appert, in the early 19th century. He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass and then heated them in boiling water to cook the contents. Appert's method had great advantages over older methods of food preservation: it could be applied to a wide range of foods, and the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products. His idea was soon copied by an Englishman, Peter Durand. Until this point, containers had been too heavy to be widely used, but Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage. Two years later, in 1812, two Englishmen, Bryan Donkin and John Hall, started the commercial canning of food, although the real rise in popularity of canning had to wait until the invention of the can opener in 1855. Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer. Canning is an extremely effective way of preserving food: one can containing meat, dating back to 1824, was opened in 1939, and the contents were still in good condition.
 
(F) In the 21st century, the dominance of canning as a method of food preservation has been overtaken by freezing. Chilling food to keep it fresh is an old idea. The earliest mentions of icehouses, thick-walled buildings, half underground, date back to 1700 BC in northwest Iran. In early 16th-century Italy, water was mixed with chemicals to lower its freezing point to -18 degrees Celsius. Several centuries later, frozen fish and other goods were transported by ship from Australia to England. However, the modern frozen food industry was started in the 1920s by an American, Clarence Birdseye. While on a fishing trip with the Inuit in the Canadian Arctic, Birdseye observed that rapid freezing creates smaller ice crystals and therefore causes less damage to food—a discovery he had not expected. Nevertheless, the major growth in demand for frozen food came with the arrival of freezers in ordinary people's homes. The advantages of frozen over canned food include the fact that the flavor and consistency are often identical to the fresh product, and freezing can be used to preserve a wide variety of foods.

questions.question: According to Darwin, cooking was the most significant development in human history.

analyses.content: 题目中的“the most significant”忽略了原文的限定词“after language”。
(Paragraph A) “...cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man.”
题目说根据达尔文，烹饪是人类历史上**最重要（most significant）**的发展。原文A段说达尔文认为烹饪是“after language, was the greatest discovery（仅次于语言的最伟大发现）”，即语言才是第一，烹饪第二，所以不是“最重要”，选 FALSE。

questions.question: The process of cooking gets rid of some plant poisons.

analyses.content: 题目说烹饪过程会去除一些植物毒素。原文A段提到烹饪通过“destroying toxic chemicals（破坏有毒化学物质）”将不可食用的植物变成可食用的，选 TRUE。
“Gets rid of” 对应 “destroying”，“poisons” 对应 “toxic chemicals”。
(Paragraph A) “Cooking can turn plants... by destroying toxic chemicals...”

questions.question: Eating cooked food is more energy efficient than eating raw food.

analyses.content: 题目说吃熟食比吃生食更节能（energy efficient）。原文B段末尾说由于烹饪节省了咀嚼和消化的能量，身体获得的能量与消耗的能量之比在吃熟食时“is greater（更大）”，即更高效，选 TRUE。
“More energy efficient” 对应 “ratio of energy gained to energy expended... is greater”。
(Paragraph B) “...so the ratio of energy gained to energy expended... is greater when food is cooked.”

questions.question: Clarence Birdseye had previously worked in the Australian food industry.

analyses.content: 不要把“提到澳大利亚”和“提到Birdseye”强行关联，文中两者无交集。
题目说Clarence Birdseye此前曾在澳大利亚食品工业工作。原文F段虽然提到了从澳大利亚运冷冻鱼到英国（transported from Australia），但这是在他出场之前的历史背景描述，并未提及Birdseye本人是否在澳大利亚工作过，选 NOT GIVEN。
(Paragraph F) “Several centuries later, frozen fish... from Australia... However, the modern frozen food industry was started... by... Clarence Birdseye.”

questions.question: Birdseye's trip with the Inuit confirmed what he already believed about rapid freezing.

analyses.content: 题目说Birdseye与因纽特人的旅行证实了他**已经相信（already believed）**的关于快速冷冻的看法。原文F段说这是一个“discovery he had not expected（他未曾预料到的发现）”，即他之前并不相信或知道，选 FALSE。
“Confirmed what he already believed” 与 “had not expected” 矛盾。
(Paragraph F) “...a discovery he had not expected.”

analyses.content: 题目说农业带来的变化包括设备的发展和更大的____。原文C段提到人们开始制造新工具，随之“populations increased in size（人口规模增加）”，即更大的人口，填 populations。
“Larger” 对应 “increased in size”。
(Paragraph C) “...and, in turn, populations increased in size.”
(Paragraph C) “...writing ... allowed people to maintain records of the harvest and taxes.”
“Keep” 对应 “maintain”。
题目说随着书写的发展，能够保存____。原文C段提到书写变得复杂，允许人们“maintain records（保存记录）”，填 records。
题目说早期食物保存方法包括烟熏、干燥和将食物与酸或____结合。原文D段列举了方法：smoking, drying, adding acid... or adding salt，填 salt。
并列关系，直接定位列举项。
(Paragraph D) “...smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt.”
题目说Nicolas Appert把食物放进由____制成的容器中。原文E段提到他把食物密封在“bottles fabricated from glass（由玻璃制成的瓶子）”中，填 glass。
“Made of” 对应 “fabricated from”。
(Paragraph E) “He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass...”
(Paragraph E) “...the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products.”
题目说Appert的方法使保存的食物具有��新鲜食物相同的味道和____。原文E段说“flavor and texture were similar（风味和质地相似）”，填 texture。
“Taste” 对应 “flavor”，“same/similar” 对应。
题目说Peter Durand引入了罐头，优点是____且不易破碎。原文E段提到Durand生产了第一批“lightweight（轻便的）”且抗损坏的容器，填 lightweight。
“Hard to break” 对应 “resistant to damage”，并列的是 “lightweight”。
(Paragraph E) “...Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage.”
题目说1855年，金属开罐器取代了曾与锤子一起使用的____。原文E段提到在此之前，罐头是用“chisel（凿子）”和锤子打开的，填 chisel。
“Replaced” 意味着找之前的工具，原文 “Until then, cans were opened with...”。
(Paragraph E) “Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer.”
题目说一百多年后仍可食用，例如一罐旧的____。原文E段末尾提到一罐含有“meat（肉）”的罐头（1824年产，1939年开），填 meat。
“Can of” 对应 “can containing”。
(Paragraph E) “...one can containing meat, dating back to 1824...”
